title: The CHER Ending
kidRule: When a word ends with a 'cher' sound, like NATURE, it is usually spelled T-U-R-E. The T and the U team up to make the 'ch' sound!
hint: Listen to the 'cher' sound at the end. It is not spelled the way it sounds! Which four letters make that ending?
reminder: The 'cher' sound at the end of this word is spelled T-U-R-E.

check.question: Why does NATURE end with T-U-R-E?
check.correctAnswer: Because the 'cher' sound at the end of a word is usually spelled T-U-R-E!
distractors: Because every word about the outdoors ends with T-U-R-E
Because the E at the end is only there to make the word look longer

words.def: Everything in the world that was not made by people, like plants, animals, weather, and mountains.
words.sent: We took a walk to enjoy nature and listen to the birds.
words.story: Spending time in nature is good for you: studies show that being around trees can help people feel calmer!
words.card: Look *at* that! In *nature*, even the snails use the slow lane!

words.def: The time that has not happened yet.
words.sent: In the future, I want to be a pilot.
words.story: A time capsule buried at the 1939 World's Fair in New York is a message to the future: it is not supposed to be opened until the year 6939!
words.card: In the *future*, robots will have *fu*n teaching cats to dance!

words.def: An exciting trip or time when you do new and daring things.
words.sent: Our hike to the waterfall was a real adventure.
words.story: The word comes from a Latin word that means 'something about to happen'!
words.card: The hamster crawled through the air *vent* on a daring *adventure* to find cheese!

words.def: Any living animal, big or small.
words.sent: A tiny creature with eight legs crawled under the leaf.
words.story: The blue whale is the biggest creature that has ever lived, even bigger than the biggest dinosaurs!
words.card: Every *creature* in the pond came to *eat* my sandwich!

words.def: Something made by stirring different things together.
words.sent: Pour the cake mixture into the pan.
words.story: The air you breathe is a mixture of gases, and only about one fifth of it is oxygen!
words.card: I *mix* mud and glitter to make a magic *mixture* for trolls!

words.def: Your own name, written by you in your own special way.
words.sent: The author wrote her signature inside my book.
words.story: John Hancock wrote his name so large on the Declaration of Independence that Americans still call a signature a 'John Hancock'!
words.card: Please *sign* your *signature* on my cast with a purple pen!

words.def: To catch something and keep it from getting away.
words.sent: We tried to capture a firefly in a jar.
words.story: A Venus flytrap can capture a bug by snapping shut in less than one second!
words.card: I used my baseball *cap* to *capture* a runaway meatball!

words.def: A large bird that eats animals that have already died.
words.sent: A vulture circled high above the desert.
words.story: Vultures are nature's cleanup crew, and their stomach juice is strong enough to destroy dangerous germs!
words.card: The *vulture* invited a *tur*key to tea and served bone soup!

words.def: Things like chairs, tables, and beds that people use in a room.
words.sent: We moved all the furniture to make room for dancing.
words.story: At Skara Brae in Scotland you can still see stone furniture, like beds and shelves, that is about 5,000 years old!
words.card: The cat left so much *fur* on the *furniture* that the sofa looked like a bear!

words.def: How hot or cold something is.
words.sent: The temperature dropped and the puddles turned to ice.
words.story: The coldest temperature ever measured on Earth was about 128 degrees below zero Fahrenheit, in Antarctica!
words.card: A *rat* with a thermometer checked the *temperature* of my soup!
